paragraphs.text: And as he went forth out of the temple, one of his disciples saith unto him, Teacher, behold, what manner of stones and what manner of buildings!
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἐκπορευομένου αὐτοῦ ἐκ τοῦ ἱεροῦ λέγει αὐτῷ εἷς τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ· Διδάσκαλε, ἴδε ποταποὶ λίθοι καὶ ποταπαὶ οἰκοδομαί.
paragraphs.translit: Kai ekporeuomenou autou ek tou hierou legei autō heis tōn mathētōn autou· Didaskale, ide potapoi lithoi kai potapai oikodomai.

paragraphs.text: And Jesus said unto him, Seest thou these great buildings? there shall not be left here one stone upon another, which shall not be thrown down.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Βλέπεις ταύτας τὰς μεγάλας οἰκοδομάς; οὐ μὴ ἀφεθῇ ὧδε λίθος ἐπὶ λίθον ὃς οὐ μὴ καταλυθῇ.
paragraphs.translit: kai ho Iēsous eipen autō· Blepeis tautas tas megalas oikodomas; ou mē aphethē hōde lithos epi lithon hos ou mē katalythē.

paragraphs.text: And as he sat on the mount of Olives over against the temple, Peter and James and John and Andrew asked him privately,
paragraphs.original: Καὶ καθημένου αὐτοῦ εἰς τὸ Ὄρος τῶν Ἐλαιῶν κατέναντι τοῦ ἱεροῦ ἐπηρώτα αὐτὸν κατʼ ἰδίαν Πέτρος καὶ Ἰάκωβος καὶ Ἰωάννης καὶ Ἀνδρέας·
paragraphs.translit: Kai kathēmenou autou eis to Oros tōn Elaiōn katenanti tou hierou epērōta auton katʼ idian Petros kai Iakōbos kai Iōannēs kai Andreas·

paragraphs.text: Tell us, when shall these things be? and what [shall be] the sign when these things are all about to be accomplished?
paragraphs.original: Εἰπὸν ἡμῖν πότε ταῦτα ἔσται, καὶ τί τὸ σημεῖον ὅταν μέλλῃ ταῦτα συντελεῖσθαι πάντα.
paragraphs.translit: Eipon hēmin pote tauta estai, kai ti to sēmeion hotan mellē tauta synteleisthai panta.

paragraphs.text: And Jesus began to say unto them, Take heed that no man lead you astray.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἤρξατο λέγειν αὐτοῖς· Βλέπετε μή τις ὑμᾶς πλανήσῃ·
paragraphs.translit: ho de Iēsous ērxato legein autois· Blepete mē tis hymas planēsē·

paragraphs.text: Many shall come in my name, saying, I am [he]; and shall lead many astray.
paragraphs.original: πολλοὶ ἐλεύσονται ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματί μου λέγοντες ὅτι Ἐγώ εἰμι, καὶ πολλοὺς πλανήσουσιν.
paragraphs.translit: polloi eleusontai epi tō onomati mou legontes hoti Egō eimi, kai pollous planēsousin.

paragraphs.text: And when ye shall hear of wars and rumors of wars, be not troubled: [these things] must needs come to pass; but the end is not yet.
paragraphs.original: ὅταν δὲ ἀκούσητε πολέμους καὶ ἀκοὰς πολέμων, μὴ θροεῖσθε· δεῖ γενέσθαι, ἀλλʼ οὔπω τὸ τέλος.
paragraphs.translit: hotan de akousēte polemous kai akoas polemōn, mē throeisthe· dei genesthai, allʼ oupō to telos.

paragraphs.text: For nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom; there shall be earthquakes in divers places; there shall be famines: these things are the beginning of travail.
paragraphs.original: ἐγερθήσεται γὰρ ἔθνος ἐπʼ ἔθνος καὶ βασιλεία ἐπὶ βασιλείαν, ἔσονται σεισμοὶ κατὰ τόπους, ἔσονται λιμοί· ἀρχὴ ὠδίνων ταῦτα.
paragraphs.translit: egerthēsetai gar ethnos epʼ ethnos kai basileia epi basileian, esontai seismoi kata topous, esontai limoi· archē ōdinōn tauta.

paragraphs.text: But take ye heed to yourselves: for they shall deliver you up to councils; and in synagogues shall ye be beaten; and before governors and kings shall ye stand for my sake, for a testimony unto them.
paragraphs.original: βλέπετε δὲ ὑμεῖς ἑαυτούς· παραδώσουσιν ὑμᾶς εἰς συνέδρια καὶ εἰς συναγωγὰς δαρήσεσθε καὶ ἐπὶ ἡγεμόνων καὶ βασιλέων σταθήσεσθε ἕνεκεν ἐμοῦ εἰς μαρτύριον αὐτοῖς.
paragraphs.translit: blepete de hymeis heautous· paradōsousin hymas eis synedria kai eis synagōgas darēsesthe kai epi hēgemonōn kai basileōn stathēsesthe heneken emou eis martyrion autois.

paragraphs.text: And the gospel must first be preached unto all the nations.
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἰς πάντα τὰ ἔθνη πρῶτον δεῖ κηρυχθῆναι τὸ εὐαγγέλιον.
paragraphs.translit: kai eis panta ta ethnē prōton dei kērychthēnai to euangelion.

paragraphs.text: And when they lead you [to judgment], and deliver you up, be not anxious beforehand what ye shall speak: but whatsoever shall be given you in that hour, that speak ye; for it is not ye that speak, but the Holy Spirit.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ὅταν ἄγωσιν ὑμᾶς παραδιδόντες, μὴ προμεριμνᾶτε τί λαλήσητε, ἀλλʼ ὃ ἐὰν δοθῇ ὑμῖν ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ὥρᾳ τοῦτο λαλεῖτε, οὐ γάρ ἐστε ὑμεῖς οἱ λαλοῦντες ἀλλὰ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον.
paragraphs.translit: kai hotan agōsin hymas paradidontes, mē promerimnate ti lalēsēte, allʼ ho ean dothē hymin en ekeinē tē hōra touto laleite, ou gar este hymeis hoi lalountes alla to pneuma to hagion.

paragraphs.text: And brother shall deliver up brother to death, and the father his child; and children shall rise up against parents, and cause them to be put to death.
paragraphs.original: καὶ παραδώσει ἀδελφὸς ἀδελφὸν εἰς θάνατον καὶ πατὴρ τέκνον, καὶ ἐπαναστήσονται τέκνα ἐπὶ γονεῖς καὶ θανατώσουσιν αὐτούς·
paragraphs.translit: kai paradōsei adelphos adelphon eis thanaton kai patēr teknon, kai epanastēsontai tekna epi goneis kai thanatōsousin autous·

paragraphs.text: And ye shall be hated of all men for my name`s sake: but he that endureth to the end, the same shall be saved.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἔσεσθε μισούμενοι ὑπὸ πάντων διὰ τὸ ὄνομά μου. ὁ δὲ ὑπομείνας εἰς τέλος οὗτος σωθήσεται.
paragraphs.translit: kai esesthe misoumenoi hypo pantōn dia to onoma mou. ho de hypomeinas eis telos houtos sōthēsetai.

paragraphs.text: But when ye see the abomination of desolation standing where he ought not (let him that readeth understand), then let them that are in Judaea flee unto the mountains:
paragraphs.original: Ὅταν δὲ ἴδητε τὸ βδέλυγμα τῆς ἐρημώσεως ἑστηκότα ὅπου οὐ δεῖ, ὁ ἀναγινώσκων νοείτω, τότε οἱ ἐν τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ φευγέτωσαν εἰς τὰ ὄρη,
paragraphs.translit: Hotan de idēte to bdelygma tēs erēmōseōs hestēkota hopou ou dei, ho anaginōskōn noeitō, tote hoi en tē Ioudaia pheugetōsan eis ta orē,

paragraphs.text: and let him that is on the housetop not go down, nor enter in, to take anything out his house:
paragraphs.original: ὁ ἐπὶ τοῦ δώματος μὴ καταβάτω μηδὲ εἰσελθάτω τι ἆραι ἐκ τῆς οἰκίας αὐτοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: ho epi tou dōmatos mē katabatō mēde eiselthatō ti arai ek tēs oikias autou,

paragraphs.text: and let him that is in the field not return back to take his cloak.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ὁ εἰς τὸν ἀγρὸν μὴ ἐπιστρεψάτω εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω ἆραι τὸ ἱμάτιον αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai ho eis ton agron mē epistrepsatō eis ta opisō arai to himation autou.

paragraphs.text: But woe unto them that are with child and to them that give suck in those days!
paragraphs.original: οὐαὶ δὲ ταῖς ἐν γαστρὶ ἐχούσαις καὶ ταῖς θηλαζούσαις ἐν ἐκείναις ταῖς ἡμέραις.
paragraphs.translit: ouai de tais en gastri echousais kai tais thēlazousais en ekeinais tais hēmerais.

paragraphs.text: And pray ye that it be not in the winter.
paragraphs.original: προσεύχεσθε δὲ ἵνα μὴ γένηται χειμῶνος·
paragraphs.translit: proseuchesthe de hina mē genētai cheimōnos·

paragraphs.text: For those days shall be tribulation, such as there hath not been the like from the beginning of the creation which God created until now, and never shall be.
paragraphs.original: ἔσονται γὰρ αἱ ἡμέραι ἐκεῖναι θλῖψις οἵα οὐ γέγονεν τοιαύτη ἀπʼ ἀρχῆς κτίσεως ἣν ἔκτισεν ὁ θεὸς ἕως τοῦ νῦν καὶ οὐ μὴ γένηται.
paragraphs.translit: esontai gar hai hēmerai ekeinai thlipsis hoia ou gegonen toiautē apʼ archēs ktiseōs hēn ektisen ho theos heōs tou nyn kai ou mē genētai.

paragraphs.text: And except the Lord had shortened the days, no flesh would have been saved; but for the elect`s sake, whom he chose, he shortened the days.
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἰ μὴ ἐκολόβωσεν κύριος τὰς ἡμέρας, οὐκ ἂν ἐσώθη πᾶσα σάρξ. ἀλλὰ διὰ τοὺς ἐκλεκτοὺς οὓς ἐξελέξατο ἐκολόβωσεν τὰς ἡμέρας.
paragraphs.translit: kai ei mē ekolobōsen kyrios tas hēmeras, ouk an esōthē pasa sarx. alla dia tous eklektous hous exelexato ekolobōsen tas hēmeras.

paragraphs.text: And then if any man shall say unto you, Lo, here is the Christ; or, Lo, there; believe [it] not:
paragraphs.original: καὶ τότε ἐάν τις ὑμῖν εἴπῃ· Ἴδε ὧδε ὁ χριστός, Ἴδε ἐκεῖ, μὴ πιστεύετε·
paragraphs.translit: kai tote ean tis hymin eipē· Ide hōde ho christos, Ide ekei, mē pisteuete·

paragraphs.text: for there shall arise false Christs and false prophets, and shall show signs and wonders, that they may lead astray, if possible, the elect.
paragraphs.original: ἐγερθήσονται γὰρ ψευδόχριστοι καὶ ψευδοπροφῆται καὶ δώσουσιν σημεῖα καὶ τέρατα πρὸς τὸ ἀποπλανᾶν εἰ δυνατὸν τοὺς ἐκλεκτούς·
paragraphs.translit: egerthēsontai gar pseudochristoi kai pseudoprophētai kai dōsousin sēmeia kai terata pros to apoplanan ei dynaton tous eklektous·

paragraphs.text: But take ye heed: behold, I have told you all things beforehand.
paragraphs.original: ὑμεῖς δὲ βλέπετε· προείρηκα ὑμῖν πάντα.
paragraphs.translit: hymeis de blepete· proeirēka hymin panta.

paragraphs.text: But in those days, after that tribulation, the sun shall be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light,
paragraphs.original: Ἀλλὰ ἐν ἐκείναις ταῖς ἡμέραις μετὰ τὴν θλῖψιν ἐκείνην ὁ ἥλιος σκοτισθήσεται, καὶ ἡ σελήνη οὐ δώσει τὸ φέγγος αὐτῆς,
paragraphs.translit: Alla en ekeinais tais hēmerais meta tēn thlipsin ekeinēn ho hēlios skotisthēsetai, kai hē selēnē ou dōsei to phengos autēs,

paragraphs.text: and the stars shall be falling from heaven, and the powers that are in the heavens shall be shaken.
paragraphs.original: καὶ οἱ ἀστέρες ἔσονται ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ πίπτοντες, καὶ αἱ δυνάμεις αἱ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς σαλευθήσονται.
paragraphs.translit: kai hoi asteres esontai ek tou ouranou piptontes, kai hai dynameis hai en tois ouranois saleuthēsontai.

paragraphs.text: And then shall they see the Son of man coming in clouds with great power and glory.
paragraphs.original: καὶ τότε ὄψονται τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐρχόμενον ἐν νεφέλαις μετὰ δυνάμεως πολλῆς καὶ δόξης·
paragraphs.translit: kai tote opsontai ton hyion tou anthrōpou erchomenon en nephelais meta dynameōs pollēs kai doxēs·

paragraphs.text: And then shall he send forth the angels, and shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from the uttermost part of the earth to the uttermost part of heaven.
paragraphs.original: καὶ τότε ἀποστελεῖ τοὺς ἀγγέλους καὶ ἐπισυνάξει τοὺς ἐκλεκτοὺς ἐκ τῶν τεσσάρων ἀνέμων ἀπʼ ἄκρου γῆς ἕως ἄκρου οὐρανοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai tote apostelei tous angelous kai episynaxei tous eklektous ek tōn tessarōn anemōn apʼ akrou gēs heōs akrou ouranou.

paragraphs.text: Now from the fig tree learn her parable: when her branch is now become tender, and putteth forth its leaves, ye know that the summer is nigh;
paragraphs.original: Ἀπὸ δὲ τῆς συκῆς μάθετε τὴν παραβολήν· ὅταν ἤδη ὁ κλάδος αὐτῆς ἁπαλὸς γένηται καὶ ἐκφύῃ τὰ φύλλα, γινώσκετε ὅτι ἐγγὺς τὸ θέρος ἐστίν·
paragraphs.translit: Apo de tēs sykēs mathete tēn parabolēn· hotan ēdē ho klados autēs hapalos genētai kai ekphyē ta phylla, ginōskete hoti engys to theros estin·

paragraphs.text: even so ye also, when ye see these things coming to pass, know ye that he is nigh, [even] at the doors.
paragraphs.original: οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς, ὅταν ἴδητε ταῦτα γινόμενα, γινώσκετε ὅτι ἐγγύς ἐστιν ἐπὶ θύραις.
paragraphs.translit: houtōs kai hymeis, hotan idēte tauta ginomena, ginōskete hoti engys estin epi thyrais.

paragraphs.text: Verily I say unto you, This generation shall not pass away, until all these things be accomplished.
paragraphs.original: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐ μὴ παρέλθῃ ἡ γενεὰ αὕτη μέχρις οὗ ταῦτα πάντα γένηται.
paragraphs.translit: amēn legō hymin hoti ou mē parelthē hē genea hautē mechris hou tauta panta genētai.

paragraphs.text: Heaven and earth shall pass away: but my words shall not pass away.
paragraphs.original: ὁ οὐρανὸς καὶ ἡ γῆ παρελεύσονται, οἱ δὲ λόγοι μου οὐ μὴ παρελεύσονται.
paragraphs.translit: ho ouranos kai hē gē pareleusontai, hoi de logoi mou ou mē pareleusontai.

paragraphs.text: But of that day or that hour knoweth no one, not even the angels in heaven, neither the Son, but the Father.
paragraphs.original: Περὶ δὲ τῆς ἡμέρας ἐκείνης ἢ τῆς ὥρας οὐδεὶς οἶδεν, οὐδὲ οἱ ἄγγελοι ἐν οὐρανῷ οὐδὲ ὁ υἱός, εἰ μὴ ὁ πατήρ.
paragraphs.translit: Peri de tēs hēmeras ekeinēs ē tēs hōras oudeis oiden, oude hoi angeloi en ouranō oude ho hyios, ei mē ho patēr.

paragraphs.text: Take ye heed, watch and pray: for ye know not when the time is.
paragraphs.original: βλέπετε ἀγρυπνεῖτε, οὐκ οἴδατε γὰρ πότε ὁ καιρός ἐστιν·
paragraphs.translit: blepete agrypneite, ouk oidate gar pote ho kairos estin·

paragraphs.text: [It is] as [when] a man, sojourning in another country, having left his house, and given authority to his servants, to each one his work, commanded also the porter to watch.
paragraphs.original: ὡς ἄνθρωπος ἀπόδημος ἀφεὶς τὴν οἰκίαν αὐτοῦ καὶ δοὺς τοῖς δούλοις αὐτοῦ τὴν ἐξουσίαν, ἑκάστῳ τὸ ἔργον αὐτοῦ, καὶ τῷ θυρωρῷ ἐνετείλατο ἵνα γρηγορῇ.
paragraphs.translit: hōs anthrōpos apodēmos apheis tēn oikian autou kai dous tois doulois autou tēn exousian, hekastō to ergon autou, kai tō thyrōrō eneteilato hina grēgorē.

paragraphs.text: Watch therefore: for ye know not when the lord of the house cometh, whether at even, or at midnight, or at cockcrowing, or in the morning;
paragraphs.original: γρηγορεῖτε οὖν, οὐκ οἴδατε γὰρ πότε ὁ κύριος τῆς οἰκίας ἔρχεται, ἢ ὀψὲ ἢ μεσονύκτιον ἢ ἀλεκτοροφωνίας ἢ πρωΐ,
paragraphs.translit: grēgoreite oun, ouk oidate gar pote ho kyrios tēs oikias erchetai, ē opse ē mesonyktion ē alektorophōnias ē prōi,

paragraphs.text: lest coming suddenly he find you sleeping.
paragraphs.original: μὴ ἐλθὼν ἐξαίφνης εὕρῃ ὑμᾶς καθεύδοντας·
paragraphs.translit: mē elthōn exaiphnēs heurē hymas katheudontas·

paragraphs.text: And what I say unto you I say unto all, Watch.
paragraphs.original: ὃ δὲ ὑμῖν λέγω πᾶσιν λέγω· γρηγορεῖτε.
paragraphs.translit: ho de hymin legō pasin legō· grēgoreite.
